config.title: Build typed modal manager API

intro.title: Build typed modal manager API
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed modal manager API in TypeScript to manage pop-up windows in a web application. You'll learn how to use TypeScript's type system to create a safe, reusable system for opening and closing modals. The core concepts involve defining custom types, using generics for flexibility, and structuring a class-based API. By the end, you'll have a fully typed manager that prevents common errors and improves code maintainability.
intro.usecase: A typed modal manager API is essential in modern web applications like admin dashboards, e-commerce platforms, and SaaS tools, where users frequently interact with modals for actions such as editing profiles, confirming purchases, or configuring settings. For example, in a project management app like Asana or Trello, developers use this pattern to manage task-creation modals, attachment previews, and team invitation dialogs with strict type safety. This ensures that each modal receives the correct props—like a task title or user ID—preventing runtime errors and improving developer experience when adding new modal types across large codebases.

objectives: Implement a TypeScript interface to define the structure of a modal configuration
Construct a typed modal manager class with methods for opening and closing modals
Apply generic types to create reusable modal components with different content types
Initialize and manage modal state using TypeScript's type system for safety
Configure event handlers for modal interactions with proper type annotations
Integrate the modal manager into a TypeScript application with type-safe API calls
Manipulate modal visibility and content through typed method implementations

steps.title: Import TypeScript types and create ModalConfig interface
steps.instruction: Create a ModalConfig interface with id (string), title (string), content (string), and isOpen (boolean) properties.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define each property with its type annotation.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ModalConfig interface with typed properties will be created as the foundation for modal configuration.
successCriteria: ModalConfig interface exists with id: string, title: string, content: string, and isOpen: boolean properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.hint: Use the find method on the modals array to locate the modal by id, then update its isOpen property.

successCriteria: A private isModalConfig method exists in the ModalManager class that returns a boolean and validates the required properties.
